newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain petrol stations see no solution with govt.
newsitem.headline: Spain petrol stations see no solution with govt.

text.p: Spanish petrol stations are pessimistic about solving a row with the government over a deal to allow truckers' cooperatives to buy diesel directly from suppliers.
"The doors (to a solution) are closing," said Roberto Sanz, chairman of service stations confederation CEES on Wednesday.
The group was not ruling out a strike by service station owners.

In comments quoted by local media, Sanz said it seemed the government did not want to negotiate with the sector, which he said was the most affected by the measures to cheapen fuel for truckers' cooperatives.
"(The move) will cause job losses of around 10,000 and will affect investment of over half a trillion pesetas in the last few years," he added.
Earlier this month the government approved a decree to save transport cooperatives five to 10 pesetas per litre on diesel, in response to a two week truckers' strike.
